column1: # Batch 34 — ndjson: what the new mode still does not reach, kept as data.

column3: https://index.crates.io/<shard>/<shard>/<name> — probed live and PASS as ndjson (316 version lines for serde, 164874 bytes), and strictly richer than the crates.io web API's version list: each line carries the version's COMPLETE deps list with semver reqs, feature lists, optional/default_features flags, target cfg and kind, plus the features map, links, yanked flag, rust_version, the sha-256 cksum and pubtime. One request replaces the hundreds the web API needs for the same dependency history. It still cannot ship as a row, because the path is SHARDED BY CRATE NAME and in four different layouts: a 1-character name lives at /1/<name>, 2 characters at /2/<name>, 3 at /3/<first>/<name>, and 4 or more at /<chars 1-2>/<chars 3-4>/<name>. An entity pivot would have to compute that, and a declarative row cannot hold code — the same reason CLAUDE.md gives for not converting VJSON_PREP. Hardcoding one shard (as the probe URL does) yields a row that answers only about crates whose names begin with those two characters and 404s for every other, which is an honest empty but a useless source. Fixing it properly means either substring tokens in hp_expand plus a way to express the length branching, or a hand-written run() like geo_tidesandcurrents_currents.

This entry was WRONG and the row shipped in batch 35. It claimed an array of bare STRINGS was unregisterable because lib/hpengine.c counts a bare scalar in a JSON array as an `empty` slot. That is true of a NULL, a number or an empty string — a trailing newline — and NOT of a string with content: hp_json_flat() already maps one to {"value": "<the string>"}, so title_keys=value;id_keys=value is all such a row needs. Measured 2026-10-05: MCR_IMAGE_CATALOG emitted 3851 of 3851 and stored 3851. The same correction applies to the three endpoints this entry dragged down with it — api.nuget.org/v3-flatcontainer (86 of 86 stored), pub.dev/api/package-names (91388 of 91388) and packagist.org/packages/list.json — all four are in docs/candidate-sources-batch35.strings.txt. The lesson is the one this repo keeps relearning: a capability claim read off a comment is not a measurement.
HTTP 401 DENIED. AWS public ECR is anonymously readable but only after a token exchange against its auth endpoint, and hpengine has no token-dance step.

The host is reachable (/m2/ and /search both answer 200) but it publishes no JSON API — /api/v1/plugins and /api/v1/search are both 404. What is there is a Maven-layout repository under /m2/, which is the same shape as the MAVENCENTRAL_PATH_LISTING row already shipped in batch 33 and would need its own directory-walk rather than one endpoint.
Reachable and live, but it is PyPI's staging instance: its contents are test uploads, not the real namespace. Registering it would add records that look like package intelligence and are not.

The row that shipped walks 20 pages of 2,000 per hourly run, which is the recent window. The index goes back to 2019-04-10 and a full walk is millions of versions; that is a backfill job, not a scheduled feed, and page_max is the honest bound with its ceiling stamped on every record when it bites.
